one of green sauce's early m3s from 2015, with a rotatable board not seen in many of their other games ([b]dreams of a geisha[/b], their first game might be the only one, plus the [b]season match[/b] series by another dev). it also offers swap, pop and chain options, another thing that got forgotten about (it's in their other early game, [b]joan of arc[/b]), these days they just reskin the same simplified m3 thing over and over. or re-release their older titles without a word about the original on the store page (e.g. geisha again).

100 levels, then 'free play' that just means a level select screen not available until then. limited/unlimited moves, pop/swap/chain can be chosen before each level but chains only work in cardinal directions, can't do diagonals. matches create unsatisfying bombs (click to trigger, can be swapped), a village to build for bonuses (mostly moves, irrelevant for unlimited play), the works. board rotation isn't limited, nor does it need to be charged. shuffle has a long cooldown and unlocked destructive power-ups need matches of certain tiles to build up.

the expected decent presentation with pretty good music, separate volumes (sfx is bugged, clicking buttons still makes a sound if muted), languages, resizable windowed mode, custom cursor, help and hint toggles. unfortunately, the end-of-level score counter can't be skipped or sped up, the continue button only appears after. buildings take unnecessarily long to build as well, gotta look at the same 3-frame animation for a while.

it's good enough for what it is if you catch it on sale, but even with all the options for gameplay, it's not as fun as I expected. rotation only does something if there are empty cells, lots of waiting around for shuffle to charge when there are no moves left, so I stuck to swapping. and even after a supposed fix, no achievements unlocked for me but I don't care about that.

An outstanding match-3 puzzle game where the player rebuilds communities with the geisha and samurai. The graphics and puzzle mechanics are very impressive; they can be played through match-3, chain or block formats - in relaxed or challenge modes. Clearly, I became "addicted" to the game perhaps 10 years ago as it is simply the type of match-3 game which cannot be stopped. Full credit to developers Green Sauce!

Por lo general, no me atraen los juegos estilo Candy Crush, pero tuve una muy buena experiencia con este juego. La temática japonesa no le viene nada mal, y la estética es muy agradable. Tanto los gráficos como la banda sonora me parecen muy adecuados. La jugabilidad es bastante sólida y funcional, aunque diría que la mayor parte de los 100 niveles son demasiado fáciles. Ojalá hubiera alguna mecánica de balanceo de, por ejemplo, la mezcla y reorganización de los objetos en pantalla, ya que fácilmente se puede explotar esto para obtener mejores resultados.

También habría sido bueno que, una vez terminas los primeros cien niveles, te permitieran volver a completarlos en sucesión con la dificultad aumentada, en ve de tener que elegir un nivel cada vez, o de tener que crear una nueva partida para mayor comodidad. Quizá un modo de niveles infinitos no le habría venido mal.

El precio lo considero adecuado, y el título divierte y relaja bastante, así que definitivamente lo recomiendo.

Fine little match-3 game. 

I love the gameplay loop of slowly building up a town with resources collected through match-3 levels, and this game utilizes that mechanic to an extent. The setting is fine and the soundtrack unexpectedly goes hard sometimes. Being able to switch up the game mode after every level keeps it a little bit more interesting.

What I don't love is how the rules seem to change on you. It's at times unpredictable where new tiles come from (ie you expect them to fall down, but instead a new tile will just appear in the empty spot), tiles used in a match don't always register as used in terms of the layers/locks it breaks, some edges at the top of the level randomly don't spawn new tiles, and I could go on. It's kind of a mess sometimes.

The challenge mode is unreasonably hard. Just play on relaxed mode.

The sound mixing is quite off, some sound effects (especially when compounded in combo moves) are straight-up uncomfortable for your ears if you play with headphones.

But really, all in all it's fine, just a nice relaxing match-3 town builder.

Rather nice Matching 3 game with an ancient Japan setting. Story is simple, you have to help geisha and samurai with rebuilding a destroyed village and protecting its citizens. Visual are nicely colorful and music sets the right relaxing atmosphere.

There are 100 levels in total, nicely varied and with different shapes. You can play in three different styles - classic swap, chain and pop. To win the level you have to collect the acquired number of items, when playing in challenge mode you have to make it in a set number of steps. To make it harder there are a lot of obstacles to break through like boxes, stones, chains or ice. Luckily you have at your disposal four kinds of power ups that can help you with a stalemate. You can also shuffle the board and even rotate it, which proved to be pretty helpful.

My only complaint goes to the "Complete 200 levels!" achievement, as it's tedious to obtain. You have to play through the whole game again… I have came back for the achievement after 5 years, so it wasn't that bad, but doing it right after the first playthrough must be really tiring. Otherwise it's a pretty and very relaxing game.

不错的三消游戏

+ 音乐！！！休闲游戏如果音乐不给力真的很难有玩下去的动力！！[strike]（虽然所有游戏都少不了好BGM的衬托）[/strike]本作的音乐配合不同宝石掉落砸破石块+箱子的炸裂声十分带感。

+ 游戏模式，说实话对于非休闲的挑战模式只有swap mode才能较为轻松的通关，而chain mod和pop mode几乎并不大相庭径，只是chain mode可以战术性的少连几个为下一步做铺垫，至于为什么相对swap mode后两种比较难就不做赘述了[spoiler] （不能互换你告诉我除了运气还有什么能解决问题？	！）[/spoiler]。至于为什么说游戏模式好，那便是可以旋转的设定，当打出一面空出的状态然后转动，那酸爽~

- 遗憾的是，除了三消以外，没有其他更多的元素了。宣传视频的故事只是一个故事而不是故事的开头，后面就没了。。。没了。。。没。。。了。。。建筑只有extra moves的作用（基本不需要用啊兄弟），多点其他要素还值这个价[spoiler]当然我是打折的时候买的（之前没入steam坑的时候有发key错过了）[/spoiler]。

- 差评中说10小时成就很恶心人的，我只想说这些人大多数是不喜欢三消的，纯挂卡有那么有意思吗，玩完一遍大概需要9-11个小时，所以我这个扣分项的不是因为这个成就。然而200level就有点过分了啊（就是再玩100关，即使是100次第一关业可以），差1个没有全成就，你说差3、4个我还真觉得一遍就够了偶尔闲的时候会来玩玩，不是强迫症也被逼死了我的天。。。

另附一点小攻略：①苦无与爆破多用于消除冰块和链子，这两种是最恶心的！！②忍刀要舍得用，尤其是最角落的一个链子和冰块[strike] 这个真的是最蛋疼的[/strike]卡你很多步。③通常情况夏，在消除某几个宝石之前之前，将这一块旋转至下部，消除之后掉落运气好的话会很爽快哦~④注意右上角shuffle按钮（充满时有音效），chain mode和pop mode可指着这个重列呢

总评：较传统但素质不错的三消游戏，旋转是一特色，遗憾没有开发出其他元素，以及最后的成就令人感到无比蛋疼。

音乐 9/10

综合 7.5/10

Mittlerweile gibt es ja Match 3 Spiele wie Sand am Meer.
Da ist es nicht unbedingt leicht ein neues Spiel auf den Markt zu bringen was sich in dieser Masse behaupten kann.
TALES OF THE ORIENT: THE RISING SUN macht da keine Ausnahme.
Und doch wartet es mit einer frischen Idee auf, die ich bisher bei Match 3 Spielen nicht gesehen habe. Möglich das es das schon gibt, aber bei den nicht wenigen die ich bisher gespielt habe war es nicht.
Und zwar das Drehen des Spielfeldes.

Wie bei jeden Match 3 Spiel regnet es verschiedene Spielsteine in unterschiedlichen Spielfeldern. Man muss mindesten 3 gleiche Steine finden, damit diese sich auflösen und den Hintergrund freier machen. Und hier gibt es drei verschiedene Modi wie man spielen möchte. Einfach durch draufklicken oder durch wechseln der Steine für neue Kombinationen oder durch das Linien Verbinden der Steine.  Wie bei den meisten Spielen dieser Art wartet das Spiel auch mit Specials auf die das Auflösen erleichtern sollen. Wenn es mal nicht mehr geht, kann man das Spielfeld drehen wodurch leer stehende Felder, die vom "Spielsteinregen" nicht erfasst wurden gefüllt werden und es neue Kombinationen ergibt. Ziel ist es, wie genannt, alle Hintergrundflächen aufzulösen .Und so spielt man sich durch die 100 (!) Level.

Aufgelockert wird das Ganze durch eine kleine Story in der Zeit des alten Japans, wo man als Samurai ein Dorf beschützen muss. Mittels erspielten Gold kann man das Dorf nach und nach aufbauen.
Die Grafik ist schön gemacht und die Musiken sind schön geworden und passen sehr gut in die Zeit des Spiels.
Durch die Möglichkeiten der Spielmodi kommt zusätzliche Abwechslung auf und auch alle Achievements lassen sich bis auf eines bis Level 100 erfüllen. Das Eine? Tja das gibts wenn man 200 Level gespielt hat, egal welches Level. Ganz ehrlich? Ich habe Level 1 dauerhaft wiederholt weil es am schnellsten geht. Gna, elendes Achievementsuchting. 

Wer mal ein neues und abwechslungsreiches Match 3 Spiel sucht ist hier bestens aufgehoben. Wer nicht, der klickt einfach weiter. :)

Mais uma bela compra na Steam, desta vez foi a vez do jogo Tales of the Orient: The Rising Sun. 

Tales of The Orient: The Rising Sun é um típico jogo de match-3 ou seja, combinar 3. Porém, ele se diferencia da maioria dos jogos do mercado deste estilo por um simples motivo: O jogo possui 3 modos diferentes de jogatina, que vou explicar neste momento: O primeiro é o clássico combinar 3 (Match-3) o segundo é Chain Mode que é parecido com o jogo 4 elements (bem avaliado aqui na Steam) e o terceiro e último modo é o Pop mode, onde basicamente o jogador clica em uma combinação e está feito.

O meu preferido é o clássico Match-3, é claro. Mas isso é um diferencial para o jogador que quer entrar no mundo do jogo e não gosta tanto assim do modo clássico, podendo assim testar as outras opções. Lembrando também que no jogo você pode virar o tabuleiro, o quê possibilidade as vezes algumas retiradas de peças e combinações que você estava precisando, mas não estava conseguindo na posição atual.

O visual do jogo é muito bonito, combinando bastante aquele clima "casual" que agrada todos os tipos de jogadores. Tudo é feito a mão e muito bonito, realmente os desenvolvedores estão de parabéns pelo belo visual do jogo.

O jogo tem sim um enredo que é contado logo no início da campanha com belas imagens e uma ótima tradução para o Português. Mas não espere nada complexo: O enredo é do tipo: Alguém atacou seu vilarejo e agora você precisa lutar para se recuperar e dar um lar as pessoas que perderam tudo, construindo tudo novamente. Isso também é um fator legal do jogo, ao longo da campanha você vai construindo várias coisas para ajudar seu povo. Apesar de não ter profundidade, combina bem com o papel do enredo que foi proposto logo no início da campanha. É simples e direto. Colete ouro, construa os lugares e é isso.

Tales of The Orient: The Rising Sun também conta com 2 modos de jogo: Casual (sem limite de tentativas) e o modo hardcore (com limites de tentativas). Eu estou jogando no modo hardcore e até o momento não tive muita dificuldade. Ou seja, é um jogo que agrada todo mundo, mas o modo casual é recomendado para pessoas não acostumadas com este tipo de jogo, é claro.

No geral, o jogo não apresentou bugs e é um game super leve, podendo rodar em qualquer PC. Não espere um enredo complexo, personagens memoráveis ou um gameplay demasiado complexo. Se você quer passar seu tempo jogando algo divertido, sem compromisso e naquelas horas de procastinação, eu diria que Tales of the Orient: The Rising Sun é um "Must-buy" pelo valor de 3,49 da sale de primavera (2015). 

Lembrando que ainda conta com conquistas bem faceis de se pegar, ou seja ... um atrativo para quem quer um jogo bem fácil de platinar, o jogo ainda oferece cartas Steam.

Sobre o preço full, tudo depende de jogador para jogador. Eu não pegaria, mas o jogo pode facilmente oferecer mais de 10 horas de jogatina, ou seja ... vale a pena? depende de você. O jogo de fato acaba ficando repetitivo e enjoa com o passar do tempo.

No geral, eu recomendo Tales of the Orient: The Rising Sun.

Gra jakich wiele tego typu (Match 3) z pewnymi wyjątkami:

- możliwość rotacji planszy o 90 stopni w obu kierunkach co powoduje spadek wielu nowych "płytek",
- możliwość zmiany trybu gry z opcji "wyzwanie" (ograniczona liczba ruchów) na "rozrywka" (nieograniczona liczba ruchów) w każdym momencie gry,
- możliwość przetasowania całej planszy co często bardzo pomaga w rozgrywce,
- prócz standardowego trybu Match 3, dostępne są również dwa inne tryby łączenia "płytek": tryb łańcucha oraz tryb grupy (min 3 płytki dla obu przypadków, tyle że płytki nie muszą się znajdować poziomo lub pionowo).


Do rozegrania mamy 100 plansz których poziom zaliczenia jest stale zwiększany (jeśli ktoś lubi zdobywać osiągnięcia to wtedy musimy rozegrać je wszystkie 2 razy, czyli wychodzi 200 poziomów).

Głównym celem jest zebranie złotych płytek dzięki którym będziemy mogli odbudować naszą wioskę, a motyw Japoński bardzo umila naszą grę. Gra warta polecenia dla miłośników Japonii.

"Tales of the Orient: The Rising Sun" można polecić każdemu miłośnikowi gier typu match 3. Gra ma przyjemną grafikę, miłą dla ucha muzykę i różną trudność poziomów. Wszystko byłoby idealne gdyby nie jedno "ale" - gra na zdobycie ostatniego osiągnięcia, które otrzymuje się za przejście 200 poziomów, czyli wszystkich w normalnym trybie gry i dodatkowo wszystkich na poziomie tzw. rozrywkowym. 

O co chodzi? Otóż grając w dodatkową setkę do ostatniego osiągnięcia warto zapisywać sobie na którym poziomie zakończyło się grę, aby później nie mieć wątpliwości od którego rozpocząć dalszą - nigdzie nie ma zapisane na którym poziomie grę się zakończyło, jedynie po ukończonym poziomie wyświetla się ile procent całości mamy ukończone. Dodatkowo po ukończeniu jednego poziomu aby zagrać w następny trzeba go szukać od pierwszej strony dostępnych poziomów, nie ma takiej możliwości jak w "normalnym" trybie gry, że od razu po ukończeniu jednego poziomu gra sama przekieruje nas do następnego poziomu. Wiem - może niepotrzebnie się czepiam, ale o ile na początku rozgrywki takie szukanie jest do przyjęcia - w dalszych dziesiątkach robi się nużące i wręcz denerwujące. 

Pomimo tych zastrzeżeń gra jest ciekawa i przyjemna, a odznaka z czajniczkiem jest prześliczna, więc jak najbardziej ją polecam :)

Tales of the Orient: The Rising Sun is a match three game that has two other types of matching modes built into the game. The game also has a story line, that is enjoyable to do as well. The main game is basically 100 levels and each level has a different board to play on. Instead of endless just matching pieces though, you are given goals to achieve to pass each level which keeps the game interesting as you go along. So checking your goals before you start is the best way to get going. 

What also makes the game more tactical in thinking is you can also turn the board to the left or right in 90 degree increments. There are four game tools that can be used as soon as they are "filled" up by matching certain pieces as you move along. One tool breaks one whole row or column that the tool is used in, one breaks a whole row and column. Making sure you know what fills each tool up can make or break you getting your board done to move on to the next level.

The story line consists of building up a village, each building you complete gives you extra moves to use when you want to. The games graphics are very beautiful and makes the game very relaxing to play. The graphics alone were a big reason I purchased the game. Getting all the achievements is not hard at all, so making 100% achievements is very do-able. This casual game gets a 7/10 from me.

A casual match 3 game. There are 100 levels each with a different game board. Each board has objectives you need to complete to move on. You can play with a certain number of moves or you can pick relaxed mode which has unlimited moves. You can choose between 3 game types- swap, chain or pop. Plus you can rotate the board. Very fun!

Восстановление происходит путём покупки разного рода зданий и сооружений (жилые дома, больница, ярмарка и т.д.) Для постройки нужны только деньги, которые будем получать в конце каждого пройденного уровня, никаких ресурсов типа руды и древесины не нужно.

К особенностям можно отнести то, что игровое поле можно вращать во всех направлениях, а перед каждым уровнем нам предлагают выбрать три варианта уничтожения фишек: перестановка, цепочка и щелчок.
Ну и композиции удачно сочетаются с геймплеем, некоторые OSTы просто-таки эпичны, начинаешь чувствовать, что делаешь действительно что-то важное и полезное для жителей ))

Tales of the Orien: The Rising Sun ist ein Typisch "Match 3" Spiel was ja nie was schlechtes ist.

Es gibt 2 Schwierigkeitsgrade Challange und Entspannt. Bei Entspannt hat man unendlich viele Züge zu Verfügung um ein Level abzuschließen und bei Challange hat man nur einen begrenzten Vorrat an Zügen die man machen kann, jedoch ist es möglich den Vorrat an Zügen zu erweitern in dem man das Gold was man am Ende einer Rune erhält in neue Gebäude investiert.

Es gibt 3 verschiedene Spielmodi: Tausch-, Kette- und Gruppenmodus.
[list]
    [*]Tausch ist der klassische Bejeweled Modus
    [*]Beim Kettenmodus muss man mindestens 3 gleiche Steine per Linie Verbinden
    [*]Im Gruppenmodus kann man nur Gruppen von gleichen Steine aufeinmal entfernen
[/list]

Die musikalische Untermalung ist sehr stimmig und berühigend wenn man gerade dabei ist die richtigen Steine abzubaun um die Missionziele zu erreichen.
Der grafische Stil ist auch recht stimmig von der Farbgestallung gelungen, nichts zu auffälliges geblinke oder sonst etwas was einen die ruhige Stimmung fast schon Zen gleich stört.

Of course people who make games want the description to be exciting and positive, but the description for this game has got to be from some other, more fun game that they forgot to make.  I picture a design meeting where they asked everyone to call out the first thing that came to mind when hearing the word "Japan".

  "Sushi!"  yelled Bob from accounting.  "Samurai!" called out Jim, the janitor.  "Good, good, keep em coming." said Jane, as she jotted down the suggestions.  "Geisha!"  "Ninja stars!"  "Rice balls!"  Excitement filled the room as more and more wonderful ideas were called out.  Suddenly Albert the night watchman called out "Happy Ending!"  The room got quiet for a minute, then everyone started to cheer.  "We're totally putting that in there, or my name isn't Jane Doe!" said Jane Doe.

   So yeah, it's about rather blandly generic, or possibly generically bland as you can get.  This game accurately depicts Japanese culture about as well as Taco Bell depicts Mexican cuisine.  Now, I must say that I'm a regular American, and I really don't care how they depict anybody, except maybe Americans.  Point is, the whole "Build an ancient Japanese village " and "Exciting adventure" thing isn't all that thrilling.

     So how about the gameplay then?  Well, the next point in the description is "Rotate the board make the best matches."  At first rotating the board sounds pretty cool, until you realize that you can just keep rotating the board until you win, with the occasional match made by you to free up some space.  There are also your typical match-3 game powerups, charged by destroying gems.  Nothing revolutionary there, except maybe the bug that prevents you from clearing certain tiles.  Yes, I know they said they fixed it, and yes, it is still happening.

   If you're a match-3 player, there are certainly other games out there better than this.  Heck, HuniePop is a far better match-3 game, albeit one attached to a whole other, less savory H game, which is not an inherently bad thing, but not for everyone.  Tales of the Orient is, despite the lovely description, rather bland.  Maybe it needs more MSG.

This is the Burger King of Match 3 games: you can have it your way.   There are 3 different ways to play:  Swap, Chain, or Pop.  Swap is the traditional match 3, as in Bejeweled, where you click on a tile, then click on a second tile to swap them and make a match.  Chain is like in Tidalis, where you use the mouse to create a path of the same type of tile and then clear them.  Pop is similar to Season Match, click on groups of 3 or more matching tiles to clear them.  Personally I prefer Swap.

There is also 2 different modes.  Challenge mode gives you a set number of moves to finish the level.  Casual gives you no limit.   

The graphics are decent.  Nice backgrounds of Japanese scenery--both day and nighttime scenes.  Let's face it, you're probably not playing this game for the cutting edge graphics, so what do you expect?!

The background music get boring after awhile.  But again, are you really playing a puzzle game for great sound?  Sure it would be nice but it's not essential.

The story is bare bones, but they keep it interesting by having you purchase buildings for your village.  The buildings do not do anything, but it makes it seem like you are making progress rather than just playing for no reason.

I highly recommend this for match 3 lovers.  You can play whatever style you prefer.
